Agenda item 3.01, proclamation honoring National Red Ribbon Week. I call on Mr. McDaniel for a proclamation. Thank you. Whereas the National Family Partnership, a national leader in drug prevention, education, and advocacy sponsored the first Red Ribbon Week in 1988 in response to the murder of DEA agent Enrique Camarena, in which angered parents and youth in communities across the country began wearing red ribbons as a symbol of their commitment to raise awareness of the violence and destruction caused by drug abuse in America.

And whereas the red ribbon program is based on scientific and evidence-based principles for substance abuse prevention and incorporates the following six prevention strategies, information dissemination, prevention education, alternative activities, community-based processes, environmental approaches and problem identification and referral and whereas the 2025 theme for Red Ribbon Week life is a puzzle solve it drug-free is a call to action emphasizing how living drug-free helps build a stronger brighter future with each positive voice fitting into the bigger picture it also serves as a reminder that every person is empowered to shape the communities around us

through positivity bravery and strength and whereas Fairfax County Public Schools is committed to fostering a safe and supportive environment that empowers students to make healthy choices through offering activities and learning experiences which focus on the many ways cannabis, alcohol, tobacco, vaping, and other drug use can negatively impact student lives including a substance abuse prevention program for students experiencing substance abuse. Whereas, and whereas the efforts of FCPS educators, counselors, and support staff are instrumental in equipping students with the knowledge and skills necessary to resist peer pressure and lead fulfilling drug-free lives, we especially commend

our substance abuse program specialists and the role they play in reaffirming a cultural wellness and resilience in our schools. Now therefore be it resolved that the Fairfax County School Board does hereby proclaim October 23rd through 31st as Red Ribbon Week in recognition of the oldest and largest drug prevention program in the nation and encourages students, families, and the Fairfax County community to unite and take a personal and visible pledge to a drug-free lifestyle.
